newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais cleared of vote-buying in landmark case.
newsitem.headline: Thais cleared of vote-buying in landmark case.

text.p: A Thai provincial court made a landmark decision on Monday when it acquitted a couple suspected of vote-buying ahead of last year's general elections, a court official said.
The charges against the two were the first for vote-buying, a practice said by political analysts and police officials to be rampant ahead of most elections.

The husband and wife, Naruepol and Prapaporn Siripanich, who had pleaded not guilty, were arrested by police in Buriram province, about 400 km (248 miles) northeast of Bangkok, on June 30, 1995, and charged with buying votes for relatives standing for election in the area.

Police recovered a total of 11 million baht (US$440,000) from the couple's house. The money had been divided into wads of 120 baht and packed into envelopes attached to the election cards of the candidates for whom they were said to be buying votes.

The Buriram court ruled that the money seized by police had yet to be used to buy votes as alleged by police, the court official said. As no wrongdoing had been committed, there was no law under which the two could be punished.
The couple, arrested by police before the last general elections on July 3, 1995, were supporters of a young turk faction within the Chart Thai party which Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa leads.
The faction, called the Therd Thai group, has about 30 members of parliament and has been rankling the premier ever since the vote-buying case came up.
Because of this case and other political differences, the faction had threatened to withhold support for Banharn when he faced a no-confidence motion from the opposition this week.
Political analysts said the court ruling could appease Therd Thai members and assure Banharn of their support when it came to the vote on the no-confidence motion.
